biography.title: Biography
biography.subtitle: The life and journey of Federico Faggin
biography.intro: Federico Faggin (born December 1, 1941 in Vicenza, Italy) is a physicist, inventor and naturalized American entrepreneur. He is known for designing the first commercial microprocessor, the Intel 4004, and for his pioneering research on the nature of consciousness.

timeline.1965: Physics degree from the University of Padua
timeline.1968: Develops MOS Silicon Gate technology at Fairchild Semiconductor
timeline.1971: Designs the first commercial microprocessor, Intel 4004
timeline.1974: Co-founds Zilog and creates the Z80 microprocessor
timeline.1986: Founds Synaptics, pioneering touchpads and touchscreens
timeline.2010: Receives the National Medal of Technology and Innovation from President Obama
timeline.2011: Founds the Federico and Elvia Faggin Foundation for consciousness research

awards.medal: National Medal of Technology and Innovation (2010)

aboutUs.title: About us
aboutUs.subtitle: The Faggin Foundation and its mission
aboutUs.missionText: The Federico and Elvia Faggin Foundation is a nonprofit organization founded in 2011 to promote scientific research on the nature of consciousness. The foundation holds that consciousness is a fundamental property of reality, not a byproduct of brain activity, and funds theoretical and experimental studies to test this hypothesis.
aboutUs.visionText: A world where science recognizes consciousness as the foundation of existence, uniting scientific rigor and inner understanding for a more complete view of reality.
aboutUs.founderText: Federico Faggin, physicist and inventor of the microprocessor, after decades of success in technology has dedicated his life to understanding consciousness. His transformative experience in 1990 led him to challenge the materialist paradigm and propose a new theory of reality.
